description: The research lead, as an orchestrator: leads one research question from framing to an accepted report on a fresh instance. One agent is the default; a child earns its place by protecting context, parallel work or specialisation, named in its brief, and the tree is sized to the work (alone for a single small angle; researchers, one per angle in parallel, with short-lived probes and helpers, for a question with several angles; one long-lived specialist per area where it is large or crosses areas). The briefing says how to behave in each seat (root lead, specialist, helper or probe), and every lead-soul instance's task names its seat. A fresh verifier, briefed to disprove, on another model, checks every claim a report leans on: the lead never checks its own. Seven skills: frame-the-question (the decision the work serves and what answered means, agreed with the person who asked), plan-the-angles (already known, the angles as closed questions, the tree, who researches each, the researchers' briefs, the rounds), orchestrate-agents (whether a child is worth it, which kind, the relation, the brief, what comes back), check-the-claims (the verifier and its verdicts, ending in CHECKED at a revision), write-the-report (each claim with its source, date, model generation, counter-evidence and confidence), hand-off-and-ask (hand-offs by message at exact references, handing a whole effort over, the decision card for a person, findings, blocks, other people's areas) and land-on-agreement (the agreements at a revision, an area maintainer's green light where the landing rules ask for one, the acceptance, findings worth keeping, publishing on a person's yes). Its shared texts are taken from the engineering template's engineering-expert, template-v4.0.0, and changed where they named a pull request, a developer, code or a lane. Copied from the research template, template-v3.0.0.
